subject: Secure development integrity package & change/secret controls (SIG follow-up)
messages:
From: Elena Park <elena.park@assessify.com>
To: jonas.weber@redwood.com
Cc: SIG Intake <sig-submissions@compliancehub.org>, security@nimbus-fin.com
Date: 2026-05-17 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: SIG follow-up: artifacts for secure development control items

Jonas,

Thanks for the quick call earlier. As a follow-up to the SIG questionnaire, Nimbus has asked us to validate a narrow set of controls related to your secure development lifecycle. Could you please provide a compact evidence package that demonstrates the following for the last 6 months (where available):

- Code review gating: PR approval policy, example PR with approvals and reviewer comments (audit trail)
- CI/CD controls: pipeline jobs that run tests, static analysis, and secret scanning; timestamps and job IDs
- Secrets management: where CI secrets are stored (ephemeral tokens vs long-lived creds), KMS rotation evidence, and any ephemeral credential design notes
- Change management: approvals for production changes, change logs, and emergency rollback runbook references

We don't need full logs for everything — redacted logs with provenance (job IDs, timestamps, PR numbers, artifact names) are fine. Please indicate any items that are still in flight and an ETA for delivery.

If you can send a single archive or a shared Drive folder that contains a manifest.txt listing what we included, that will be easiest for the assessor. Target delivery by EOD Tuesday (2026-05-18) if possible.

Best,
Elena Park
Senior Assessor, Assessify

Attachments: none

From: jonas.weber@redwood.com
To: marissa_cole@redwood.com, vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com, olga_petrov@redwood.com
Cc: 
Date: 2026-05-17 10:03:12 -0700
Subject: Fwd: SIG follow-up: artifacts for secure development control items

Team — forwarding Elena's request. Nimbus needs a tight set of artifacts by EOD Tuesday. I spoke with Elena briefly; assessor prefers a single folder with a manifest and redacted logs.

Action items (please review and confirm):
- Marissa: compile a PR-level example showing reviewer comments, approvals, and the merge timestamp. Prefer a PR that had a security fix and shows reviewer threads. Mark which files are sensitive and redact diff if needed.
- Vivek: export the CI job run for the pipeline that includes static analysis, unit tests, and the secret-scan job for the last successful prod deploy (include job IDs and timings). Redact secrets but keep job IDs and artifact names.
- Olga: attach the KMS rotation memo and the policy excerpt that outlines rotation cadence and key custodians. Also pull the change approvals for the two most recent production releases (Jira SUP IDs).

I'll assemble into a single Drive folder and include a manifest.txt. If anything cannot be provided by the deadline, call me on pager.

Jonas
Head of Platform Compliance (acting)
Redwood Inference

--- Original message attached ---

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Fwd: SIG follow-up: artifacts for secure development control items

Jonas — sending the artifacts summary below. I've uploaded the files to the Drive folder and attached two files here that the assessor can use directly.

Summary of included items (in drive folder and attached):
- PR example: PR #4721 (security/ci: fix secret-scan false-positive) — includes reviewer comments, two approvals, and the merge record. File: PR-4721-summary.txt (redacted diff, includes reviewer handles and timestamps). Link: https://github.com/redwood-inference/repo/pull/4721
- CI run: ci-run-20260516.log — pipeline job IDs: job-8819 (unit-test), job-8820 (static-analysis), job-8821 (secret-scan). The secret-scan job flags are included; secrets themselves redacted. CI job console URLs are in manifest.
- KMS rotation memo: kms-rotation-memo-2026-04.pdf (rotation completed 2026-04-03; key custodians list included).
- Change approvals: change-approval-journal-2026-05.csv (entries SUP-3419, SUP-3421 with approver, timestamp, and change type). Jira links: https://jira.redwood-inference.com/browse/SUP-3419, SUP-3421
- Additional: brief note on ephemeral CI credentials design (ephemeral-ci-keys.md) and the rollback playbook excerpt (rollback-playbook-excerpt.txt).

Notes/edge cases:
- We can't provide raw service logs that include customer data; those are redacted but provenance (timestamps, job ids, artifact names) are preserved in the CI log file.
- The PR shows that reviewers requested an extra test and that the security owner approved prior to merge. The reviewer email thread is preserved in the PR comments exported to PR-4721-summary.txt.

Attachments: PR-4721-summary.txt, ci-run-20260516.log

If that's sufficient I can finalize the manifest.txt in the Drive folder and send the share link.

—Marissa
Sr. Engineering Manager, Platform Reliability
Redwood Inference

Elena — attached is the package we discussed. I've included a manifest at the root of the Drive folder and a short README that maps each requested control to the files provided. The Drive folder contains the following (redacted where required):

- PR-4721-summary.txt — exported PR comments, approvals, and merge timestamp (redacted diff).
- ci-run-20260516.log — CI job console export with job IDs and timestamps (no secrets included).
- kms-rotation-memo-2026-04.pdf — KMS rotation summary + key custodians and rotation dates.
- change-approval-journal-2026-05.csv — CSV with SUP entries and approvers.
- ephemeral-ci-keys.md — short design note on ephemeral tokens in CI and how they're short-lived (implemented via ephemeral session tokens from KMS).
- rollback-playbook-excerpt.txt — excerpt of the emergency rollback runbook used for production incidents.

Drive link: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1XyZ-example-folder
HubSpot reference: record_87624

Jira SUPs: SUP-3419, SUP-3421 (https://jira.redwood-inference.com)

If you need unredacted logs for specific items we can schedule a three-way session with your assessor under a data access agreement; otherwise this package contains the provenance necessary for SIG review. Let me know if anything else is required or if you'd like a short walkthrough tomorrow morning.

Thanks,
Jonas Weber

Redwood Inference
